scirep__PMC13212643.pdf.h2: Conservation assessment of the selected epitopes
scirep__PMC13212643.pdf.text: Before developing a multi-epitope vaccine, 1568 protein sequences along with polyprotein reference sequence (accession no: NP_690589 ) were chosen to verify the conservation of selected CTL, HTL, and BCL epitopes. The sequences of these protein were retrieved from the NCBI Virus database (S1 File). Using the IEDB Epitope Conservancy Analysis tool with a threshold value of 100%, we checked the conservation of the selected epitopes against these sequences and found that most of the chosen epitopes have a conservation of over 90%. (Tables 2 and 3 ).

scirep__PMC13212643.pdf.h2: Analyses of population coverage of the selected epitopes
scirep__PMC13212643.pdf.text: Population coverage of selected MHC Class I and Class II alleles and their epitopes were conducted using the IEDB population coverage analysis tool. Worldwide population coverage of CTL and HTL epitopes is 84.94% and 45.47%, respectively, and the combined world population coverage of CTL and HTL is 91.79%. The highest population coverage for CTL, HTL, as well as combined CTL and HTL were found in Finland (97.11%), Cuba (64.6%), and England (98.42%), respectively. The overall population coverage of these epitopes with their binding MHC alleles in different geographical locations is shown in Fig. 2 ( S4 Table). Fig. 2 Population coverage of the most promising epitopes with their binding MHC alleles.

scirep__PMC13212643.pdf.h2: Vaccine construction and analyses of physicochemical properties
scirep__PMC13212643.pdf.text: We have constructed the CHIKV vaccine using suitable linker, adjuvant to conjugate 9 CTL, 8 HTL, and 5 BCL epitopes. The AAY linker connects the CTL to the CTL epitope and the CTL to the HTL epitope; the GPGPG linker connects the HTL to the HTL epitope and the HTL to the BCL epitope; and the KK linker binds the BCL to the BCL epitope. Also, in the N-terminal region of the vaccine, an adjuvant “beta-defensin-3” (GIINTLQKYYCRVRGGRCAVLSCLPKEEQIGKCSTRGRKCCRRKK) was conjugated by “EAAAK” linker. The overall length of the prepared vaccine was 402 amino acid residues. The diagrammatic representation of the designed vaccine construction is given in Fig. 3 . Signal peptide analysis using SignalP-4.1 confirmed the absence of a secretory signal in the vaccine construct (D-score = 0.131), indicating it is not designed for extracellular secretion (S4 Fig). This characteristic favors endogenous antigen processing and presentation via the MHC class I pathway, thereby promoting a targeted cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) response essential for clearing CHIKV-infected cells. Fig. 3 A schematic diagram of multi-epitope vaccine constructed by adjuvant, linkers and selected epitopes.

The secondary structure of the designed CHIKV vaccine was predicted using the PSIPRED server (Fig. 4 ). Analysis of secondary structure revealed random coils contributed the major part (62.69%) of designed vaccine construction, followed by alpha helix (19.65%) and beta strand (17.66%). Fig. 4 Graphical representation of the secondary structure of the designed vaccine predicted by the PSIPRED server.

scirep__PMC13212643.pdf.h2: Tertiary structure prediction, refinement and validation
scirep__PMC13212643.pdf.text: We have predicted 3D structure of the CHIKV vaccine construct using I-TASSER which gave five models with C-scores of − 1.37, − 1.22, − 2.78, − 4.17, and − 4.33, respectively. The best model was selected with C-score of -1. 4.2 and refined using GalaxyRefine tool. The model was then validated using Ramachandran plot and Z-score obtained from PROCHECK and ProSA web server, respectively (Fig. 5 ). The selected 3D model exhibited 90.3% of residues in the most favored regions, 5.2% in further allowed regions, 2.3% in generously allowed regions, and 2.3% in disallowed regions. The Z-score of the model was predicted as 4.4.12. Fig. 5 Illustration of predicted 3D structure of vaccine construct and its validation. ( A ) Predicted 3D structure by I-TASSER; ( B ) The analysis results of the Ramachandran plot of predicted 3D structure. Red zones of the plot indicate the most favored regions; dark yellow indicates the further allowed regions; light yellow indicates the generously allowed regions; and white zones indicate the disallowed regions; ( C ) ProSA-web server generated graph, displaying the Z-score of predicted 3D structure of vaccine construct.

scirep__PMC13212643.pdf.h2: Discontinuous or conformational B-cell epitope prediction

scirep__PMC13212643.pdf.text: Disulfide engineering was performed to introduce structural stability of 3D vaccine construct by reducing conformational entropy, using DbD2 server and revealed potentiality of 29 pairs of amino acids to form disulfide bonds 119 . Among these 29 amino acid pairs, only 6 pairs viz. 117VAL-120ALA, 236GLY-351LYS, 304THR-307ALA, 263TYR-266THR, 247PRO-310PRO and 108ALA-118GLY with bond energy of < 3 kcal/mol were selected to form disulfide bonds in the mutant version of vaccine construct in the DbD2 server illustrated in Fig. 6 ( S5 Table). Fig. 6 The disulfide engineering of the CHIKV vaccine construct to improve protein stability. ( A ) Original protein structure before disulfide bond formation and ( B ) Mutant protein model after disulfide bond formation. The yellow portion in the black circle area indicates the disulfide bonds.

Interaction of antigen with the immune receptors are necessary to elicit appropriate immune response 120 . Since we aimed to design a vaccine that could induce immune-sensitization against the CHIKV, molecular docking was performed between the designed vaccine construct and TLR4 (PDB ID: 4G8A) to investigate the immunostimulatory activity of the designed vaccine. We selected TLR4 as primary innate immune receptor that could elicit both innate and adaptive immune responses through recognition of pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) 121 . For docking analyses, we have used ClusPro 2.0 server which generated 29 complexes with corresponding cluster members. Out of all the docked complexes, we selected the highest interacting complex from cluster no. 3, with center score and lowest energy score of − 1105.9 kcal/mol and − 1137.2 kcal/mol, respectively. Analyses of interacting interface by PDBsum revealed 52 residues with 2189 Å 2 interface area of vaccine construct were involved in interaction with 42 residues with 2256 Å 2 interface area of TLR4 (Fig. 7 ). The interaction was strengthened by 28 hydrogen bonds, 5 salt bridges, and 242 non-bonded contacts ( S6 Table). To evaluate multi-receptor engagement, the constructed vaccine was docked against TLR2 (PDB: 2Z7X) and from the docking high-affinity binding pose was represented by Cluster 3, which exhibited the lowest energy score (–1106.6), confirming a stable and reproducible interaction suitable for broad‑spectrum immune recognition ( S7 Table). Fig. 7 The docked complex of the multi-epitope designed vaccine construct and TLR4 as well as their interaction profiles. ( A ) The docked complex (vaccine-TLR4); ( B ) Interacting residues involved in vaccine-TLR4 docked complex.

We have performed 100 ns (MD) simulation for evaluation of the physicochemical stability of the designed vaccine construct and TLR4 complex by assessing the RMSD, RMSF, Rg, and H-bond dynamics. The average RMSD for the vaccine-TLR4 complex was 4.88 Å. Though there are some fluctuations in the RMSD plot, the complex maintained a stable interaction throughout the simulation (Fig. 8 A). The structural flexibility of the vaccine-TLR4 complex at the residue level was investigated by analyses of RMSF. The mean RMSF values for vaccine and TLR4 were 3.05 Å and 1.69 Å, respectively. The interacting residues of vaccine in vaccine-TLR4 complex showed the highest fluctuation of greater than 5.5 Å while fluctuation of interacting TLR4’s residues were 3.52 Å (Fig. 8 B). The radius of gyration (Rg) computation was performed to assess the compactness of the complex structure. MD simulation analyses revealed mean Rg value of the designed vaccine-TLR4 complex was 32.19 Å, while the maximum and minimum Rg were 32.96 Å and 31.65 Å, respectively. The uniform Rg of ~ 0.55 to 0.75 Å of the vaccine-receptor complex (Fig. 8 C) indicated that the vaccine-TLR4 complex was stable. Solute–solvent hydrogen bonds were also conducted to analyze the interaction between the vaccine–TLR4 complex during molecular dynamics simulation (Fig. 8 D). The result showed an average of 1786.95 hydrogen bonds between solute and solvent, which suggests effective hydration and solvent-mediated stability during the simulation (Fig. 8 D). Fig. 8 Results of molecular dynamic simulation of docked complex for 100 ns (ns). ( A ) Root mean square deviation plot of vaccine-TLR4 complex; ( B ) Root mean square fluctuation plot of vaccine-TLR4 complex; ( C ) Radiation of gyration analysis of vaccine-TLR4 complex; ( D ) H-bond dynamics of vaccine-TLR4.

After confirming the structural stability of the CHIKV vaccine construct, its ability to simulate adaptive immune response was assessed by C-ImmSim server. Analyses of C-ImmSim result revealed that primary immune response was observed with slight increase of IgM at the beginning (Fig. 9 A). Subsequent increased secondary and tertiary immune responses were observed in terms of higher levels of IgM + IgG, IgM, IgG1 + IgG2 antibodies than the primary response with a coincided decrease in antigen levels (Fig. 9 A). Increased levels of IgM and IgG denote enhanced humoral immune response. Significant B cell population (including memory cells, multiple isotypes) was found to increase in each immune response (Fig. 9 B). In case of T cell population, both active and memory HTC were found to increased following immunization (Fig. 9 C), but active CTL progressively declined long after initial increased production. On the other hand, memory cytotoxic T cell population was gradually increased after vaccination (Fig. 9 E). Dendritic cells (Fig. 9 C) were also increased (Fig. 9 F), resulting in higher level of IFN-γ and IL-2 were detected (Fig. 9 D). These findings indicate the promising antiviral response by our proposed CHIKV vaccine construct. Fig. 9 Analyses of in silico immune simulation in inducing immune responses against the CHIKV vaccine construct. ( A ) Level of antigen and immunoglobulins after vaccination; ( B ) Active B-cell population per state; ( C ) TH Cell population per state; ( D ) Cytokine and interleukins concentration with Simpson index (D = dotted line) of immune response; ( E ) T-cytotoxic cell populations per state; ( F ) Dendritic cell population per state.

scirep__PMC13212643.pdf.h3: Codon adaptation, in silico cloning, and agarose gel electrophoresis
scirep__PMC13212643.pdf.text: After designing the primary structure of vaccine construct, we reverse translated the protein sequence into a codon-optimized DNA sequence by VectorBuilder’s Codon Optimization tool. The resulting output revealed optimal Codon Adaptation Index (CAI) of 0.93 with a GC content of 59.97%. Then using SnapGene software, we inserted the optimized vaccine sequence between EcoRI and BamHI restriction site into the E. coli pET28a (+) expression vector for cloning. Initially, the length of the pET-28a (+) expression vector was 5369 bp and after insertion of the vaccine sequence between EcoRI and BamHI restriction site, the length of the pET-28a (+) expression vector was observed to be 6586 bp (Fig. 10 A and B). The agarose gel electrophoresis of vaccine construct results in 715 bp band pattern in lane 1 (Fig. 10 C) which validated that our sequence of interest is inserted appropriately. Fig. 10 In silico cloning and agarose gel electrophoresis result conducted via SnapGene software. ( A ) pET-28a ( +) expression vector before insertion of the vaccine sequence; ( B ) Constructed vaccine sequence inserted in the expression vector, pET-28a ( +); ( C ) Agarose gel electrophoresis result of the targeted sequence (462 bp—1176 bp) of proposed vaccine.

scirep__PMC13212643.pdf.h3: Stability prediction of mRNA secondary structure of designed vaccine construct
scirep__PMC13212643.pdf.text: The DNA sequence of designed vaccine construct, obtained from VectorBuilder’s Codon Optimization Tool, was used to predict optimal mRNA secondary structure of designed vaccine construct by RNAfold web server. The calculated minimum free energy for optimal secondary structure of the vaccine, the free energy of the thermodynamic ensemble and the ensemble diversity were − 518.90 kcal/mol, − 533.29 kcal/mol and 273.68, respectively (Fig. 11 ). Fig. 11 Prediction of mRNA secondary structure of designed vaccine construct. ( A ) MFE structure; ( B ) Centroid secondary structure; ( C ) Mountain plot showing comparative relationship among MFE, thermodynamic ensemble and centroid structure of vaccine mRNA; ( D ) Plot showing positional entropy for helix (slope) and loop (plateau).

Chikungunya viral infection, one of the emerging mosquito-borne diseases, is also endemic over approximately 110 countries in Indian Ocean islands, Americas, Africa etc. 122 . Various post-viral effects like myeloneuropathy, arthritis, inflammatory myositis, and encephalitis were reported in previous studies 123 – 126 . Till date no effective licensed antiviral drug or vaccine are available to treat the CHIKV 127 . Though vector control is an effective way to control the disease, prophylactic strategy like vaccination provide protection against pathogen by stimulating immunity and therefore vaccination is considered as another effective way to control vector-borne infectious diseases 120 . Use of live pathogenic component in traditional vaccine development approach in the laboratory is associated with risk of disease and may take 15 years or more to develop a successful vaccine sometimes. Immunoinformatics provides opportunity to develop cost-effective, stable and epitope-based subunit vaccine in a short time period and advantageous over non-requirement of any pathogen involvement for this simple peptide sequences production at the laboratory level 120 , 128 . Use of multi-epitope vaccine is also advantageous over single epitope-based vaccine because of presence of both MHC Class I and II epitopes in multi-epitope vaccine to induce HTL and CTL response, respectively. Presence of B cell epitopes makes multi-epitope vaccine capable of producing antibodies. Besides that, use of adjuvant (beta–defensin-3) in multi-epitope vaccine activate primary innate immune response 82 , 129 . In recent years, immunoinformatics based approaches have been employed in the design of different epitope-based subunit vaccines 130 . Therefore, in this study, we have designed an in silico multi-epitope vaccine against the CHIKV infection because use of multiple epitopes in a designed vaccine can elicit innate, humoral and cellular immunity responses together and become very attractive strategy nowadays to prevent infection by targeting several virulence factors of the infectious agent 63 , 131 . The structural proteins were targeted to design the epitopes using the in silico methods. For this purpose, we have identified and selected antigenic polyprotein (Accession number: NP_690589 ) of virus from NCBI database to carry out the multi epitope vaccine development. Antigenic polyprotein was selected due to its better immunogenic response 98 . The initial computational prediction that the target structural polyprotein localizes to the viral capsid validates its role as a structural antigen, making it a suitable target for antibodies to neutralize the virus. Furthermore, the identification of five transmembrane helices (TMRs) within this protein is significant; these regions are often involved in viral entry and membrane fusion and can harbor epitopes crucial for generating neutralizing antibodies that block these functions. Also, we have analyzed different physicochemical properties like molecular weight (MW), theoretical pI, instability index, aliphatic index, grand average of hydropathicity (GRAVY) and half-life ( Escherichia coli ) of the selected antigenic polyprotein and found quite good results. The antigenic polyprotein was then subjected to antigenicity test and revealed the antigenic nature (antigenic score: 0.5149) of protein. Antigenic score > 0.4 was considered as antigenic nature of a protein 128 . The phylogenetic result validates NP 690,589 as a highly conserved CHIKV antigen (Supplementary Fig. 1). Consequently, epitopes sourced from this region present a strategic foundation for a multi-epitope vaccine, aiming to confer broad-spectrum and lasting protection against diverse viral strains. After antigenicity prediction, we have performed T-cell and B-cell epitope prediction in the selected antigenic polyprotein because both T-cell and B-cell are considered as two main players of adaptive immune response. After entered into the body, the antigen is presented by APCs (viz. macrophage and dendritic cell) to HTL and CTL through the MHC-II and MHC-I, respectively to activate them. Activated HTL release the required cytokines to activate CTLs and B-cells, leading to destruction of entered pathogens. Besides that, B-cell itself may also activated by direct interaction of its epitopes with particular paratopes 132 . The predicted T-cell and B-cell epitopes were then subjected to antigenicity, allergenicity and toxicity analyses. Multi epitope vaccine provides cross-protection and resistance to viral evolution by focusing on conserved epitopes 119 . To prevent autoimmunity, epitopes showed homology with human protein sequence were excluded 132 . Therefore, sequence conservancy and homology assessment of epitopes with human protein sequence were also carried out. Thus, highly conserved, antigenic, non-allergic, non-toxic, and non-homology epitopes with human protein sequences were selected to construct the desired vaccine. The epitope screening revealed 9 CTL epitopes, 8 HTL epitopes, and 5 linear B-cell epitopes were suitable for vaccine construction. In reverse vaccine design technology, this kind of epitope screening is necessary to generate intense and specific immune responses, like antibody response 121 . This strategy in vaccine designing prevents unwanted participation of the non-toxic and less allergic peptides in final vaccine construct 133 – 135 . The screened epitopes showed maximum population coverage in a large number of countries like Finland, Cuba and England, indicating usefulness of our designed vaccine against the CHIKV infection globally. The selected epitopes were combined to construct the multi-epitope vaccine using suitable linkers like “AAY”, “GPGPG” and “KK”. The linkers were used to prevent formation of new junctional epitopes 136 . Furthermore, the linkers promote immune processing and helps to present HLA-II binding epitopes 137 , 138 . To activate innate antiviral immune response, a TLR-specific adjuvant, beta-defensin-3 was added at the N-terminal end of our preliminary structured vaccine construct 121 . This adjuvant, as a TLR agonists, also modulate adaptive immune response in terms of strong induction of both T-cell and antibody-mediated reactions 82 . The physicochemical property analyses of vaccine construct revealed its non-allergenic and non-toxic nature and possesses high antigenic potential with antigenic score (0.7317) greater than 0.4 to elicit host immune response. The MW (42.12 kDa) of vaccine is < 110 kDa makes it suitable for immunization due to its easy purification and faster expression capability 119 , 139 . The alkaline nature of vaccine construct was indicated by its higher pI > 7 (9.55) 82 . The calculated aliphatic index of the vaccine construct was 77.46, indicating its higher thermostability while the instability index (24.31) of proposed vaccine was found to be < 40, making it a stable vaccine construct in standard condition 76 , 84 , 140 . The negative GRAVY value (−0.213) indicates hydrophilic nature of vaccine construct with improved solubility 82 . The confirmed absence of a secretory signal peptide in our final vaccine construct (SignalP D-score = 0.131) is a critical design feature. Biologically, this ensures the vaccine protein will be processed endogenously, favoring presentation via the MHC class I pathway. This is essential for stimulating cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs), which are required for identifying and clearing cells already infected with CHIKV. The solubility is regarded as an important physicochemical property of a vaccine for many functional and biochemical investigations 132 . The vaccine shows estimated half-life of 30 h in mammalian reticulocytes (in vitro), > 20 h in yeast (in vivo) and > 10 h in Escherichia coli (in vivo) suggests that the vaccine gets opportunity to exposed for a longer period in immune system and to elicit more immune stimulation 57 . Therefore, the proposed vaccine appeared to be suitable in terms of its physicochemical aspects. In our conservancy assessment, we utilized the IEDB Epitope Conservancy Analysis tool with a 100% identity threshold on 1568 CHIKV sequences from NCBI plus the reference polyprotein, revealing > 90% conservation for most epitopes, aligning with standard practices in epitope-based vaccine design. This approach emphasizes broad sequence representation for cross-strain applicability, with our extensive dataset (1568 entries) offering more comprehensive evaluation than typical IEDB applications in prior reports, enhancing broad protective confidence. Compared to alternative methods, such as the custom Java-based exact match frequency counting which was reported in the previous study, our IEDB-centric strategy provides efficient, threshold-based conservancy without custom coding 53 . By selecting epitopes that are perfectly conserved across diverse CHIKV isolates, we aim to mitigate the risk of vaccine escape through viral mutation, thereby designing a vaccine with the potential for durable, long-term protection, which is a critical translational goal. Being a major secondary structural contributor, random coil (62.69%) makes the vaccine construct more flexible 141 , 142 . During tertiary structure analysis, the best vaccine structure from I-TASSER was selected for refinement, quality assessment and structural validation. The resulting good quality model was then subjected to search for potential conformational B-cell epitope, present as discontinuous cluster of amino acids, proximally in the 3D structure of vaccine protein 143 . These conformational B-cell epitopes elicit strong humoral immune response against the virus 132 . Therefore, 5 conformational B-cell epitopes in our vaccine construct may also evoke neutralizing antibody response against the CHIKV. The presence of these multiple conformational epitopes in our validated 3D structure suggests the vaccine can present diverse antigenic surfaces to B cells, which is crucial for eliciting a broad and potent neutralizing antibody response in vivo. Disulfide connectivity provides conformational stability of a folded protein 128 . Therefore, we have performed disulfide engineering for 6 amino acid pairs of our modeled vaccine construct that followed the selection criteria of disulfide bond engineering to impart its stability. An appropriate vaccine should stimulate both innate and adaptive immune response 121 . It was reported that various pro-inflammatory mediators like chemokines, IFN-γ and cytokines activate both adaptive immune cells (T- and B-cells) and innate immune cells (NK cells, macrophages, dendritic cells) 144 . These inflammatory mediators are released by activation of inflammatory signaling cascade in host body due to interaction of ligands with different TLRs on some innate immune cells like macrophage, dendritic cells, monocytes 82 , 144 . Therefore, we aimed to explored the binding potential of our modeled vaccine with the cell surface TLR4 and observed significant binding (binding energy score: − 1137.2 kcal/mol) between TLR4 and the constructed modeled vaccine by performing docking study with ClusPro. This high-affinity interaction involved 52 vaccine residues (2189 Å 2 interface area) and 42 TLR4 residues (2256 Å 2 interface area), stabilized by 28 hydrogen bonds, 5 salt bridges, and 242 non-bonded contacts (PDBsum analysis), suggesting strong immunostimulatory potential and efficient triggering of innate immune signaling via TLR4 recognition of the vaccine as a PAMP mimic 101 . The extensive and stable interaction interface, supported by numerous intermolecular bonds, provides a structural basis for predicting robust TLR4 engagement, which is biologically essential for initiating the NF-κB signaling cascade and triggering the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and co-stimulatory molecules necessary for adaptive immunity. Additionally, docking with TLR2 (PDB: 2Z7X) yielded a stable complex with lowest energy score of –1106.6 kcal/mol (cluster 3), indicating multi-TLR engagement for broad-spectrum immune activation. This successful binding of vaccine with TLR4 suggests quick immune response and targeted delivery of vaccine into the host cells become easier. Proper functioning of vaccine needs stable complex formation between vaccine and immune receptors 121 . MD simulation analyses (100 ns) confirmed the compactness and stability of the vaccine-TLR4 complex, with average RMSD of 4.88 Å (indicating maintained stable interaction despite minor fluctuations), mean RMSF values of 3.05 Å (vaccine) and 1.69 Å (TLR4) reflecting moderate flexibility at interacting residues, consistent Rg (~ 32.19 Å, range 31.65–32.96 Å) demonstrating structural compactness, and an average of ~ 1787 solute–solvent hydrogen bonds supporting effective hydration and solvent-mediated stability throughout the simulation. This structural and dynamic stability is a key predictor of in vivo function, as it indicates the complex can persist long enough to effectively initiate the TLR4 signaling pathway, thereby fulfilling a core requirement for effective vaccine adjuvant activity. We have employed immune simulation for the assessment of competency of our designed construct vaccine to elicit adaptive immune response. The proposed vaccine showed extreme potential to elevate antibody titers (IgM + IgG, IgM, IgG1 + IgG2) under simulated conditions during secondary and tertiary immune responses, indicating enhanced primary immune response. Moreover, increased HTC population along with elevated IFN-γ level, observed in immune simulation experiment, boosts B cell clonal expansion and subsequent antibody production 82 , 145 . On the other hand, elevated IFN-γ level enhance antiviral immune response by macrophage activation, generation of HTC1 population and suppression of HTC2 population 146 . The simulated robust antibody response and Th1-skewed cytokine profile (high IFN-γ) are biologically predictive of two key in vivo outcomes: strong neutralizing antibody production for viral clearance and a potent cell-mediated immune response crucial for eliminating infected host cells. Therefore, our proposed vaccines effectively stimulate both adaptive and innate immune responses in simulated conditions. Codon usage related limitation of vaccine expression was controlled for its maximum synthesis in E. coli through codon optimization. CAI value between 0.8 and 1 indicates the maximum codon affinity, while optimum GC content ranging from 30 to 70% suggests stability of mRNA produced from synthetic gene 72 , 77 . The mRNA of a proposed vaccine should be stable in vivo 121 . In the codon optimization experiment, a CAI value of 0.93 and an optimum GC content of 59.97% met the selection criteria for our proposed vaccine, ensuring efficient high-level expression in E. coli . Biologically, high CAI and optimal GC content are critical for achieving sufficient vaccine protein yield in an expression system like E. coli, which is a fundamental step for subsequent in vitro protein purification and in vivo immunogenicity testing. Similar result was also reflected in mRNA secondary structural analyses where, highly negative MFE (− 518.90 kcal/mol) of optimal mRNA secondary structure of our designed vaccine again confirmed the stability of vaccine produced from its in vivo mRNA. Finally, in silico cloning of vaccine construct using pET28a (+) vector confirms its expression in E. coli cells, supporting the quick and large-scale production of our proposed vaccine.

In conclusion, in our current study, we have formulated a possible multi-epitope subunit vaccine against the CHIKV with robust cross-protection capabilities using immunoinformatics and in silico approaches. The process involved selecting a highly conserved structural polyprotein ( NP_690589 ) as the antigen source, predicting B-cell and T-cell epitopes, and rigorously screening them for antigenicity, safety, and broad population coverage. After screening the epitopes by considering physicochemical properties, antigenicity and allergenicity, non-homolog with human proteins and population coverage, final vaccine construct was prepared by prioritized 9 CTL epitopes, 8 HTL epitopes and 5 linear B-cell epitopes using suitable linkers. The designed vaccine demonstrated favorable physicochemical properties, high predicted antigenicity (score: 0.7317), and the absence of a secretory signal peptide—a key feature directing it toward endogenous processing and robust CTL induction. Crucially, our stringent conservancy analysis using a 100% identity threshold across 1568 sequences aimed to target immutable viral regions for durable protection. 3D structure of final vaccine construct was modeled and validated to analyze binding affinity with human TLR4. After confirming the stability of vaccine-TLR4 complex by MD simulation study, immune simulation of vaccine construct showed elevated and effective adaptive as well as innate immune responses. Finally, codon optimization and in silico cloning of vaccine construct revealed enhanced expression and translation efficiency of our proposed vaccine using pET28a ( +) vector in E. coli cells. Therefore, our present study proposes a multi-epitope vaccine that can conceivably be utilized as a promising prophylactic treatment option for prevention of the CHIKV infection. However, this study is entirely computational. The promising in silico results necessitate comprehensive experimental validation. Future work must include in vitro expression and purification of the vaccine protein, followed by assays to confirm its immunogenicity (e.g., lymphocyte proliferation, cytokine profiling) and safety profile. Ultimately, in vivo studies in animal models are essential to evaluate protective efficacy against CHIKV challenge, establishing the candidacy of this construct for further vaccine development.
